please provide a brief summary of your experience in data management and analysis.*
question_overrides.answer: I have built production data pipelines, quality frameworks, and analysis systems using Python, SQL, Spark, Airflow, AWS, and GCP. At EPAM, I improved Spark pipeline runtime by 50% and reduced SLA breaches by 75%; at SoFi, I modernized a workflow processing 1 TB of data into 2,000+ reports daily, improving worst-case runtime by 12x. I have also built high-volume IoT ingestion pipelines, implemented schema enforcement and anomaly detection, and developed evaluation datasets and observability workflows for AI systems.

question_overrides.pattern: please provide a brief summary of your experience using ai tools for data management.*
question_overrides.answer: I have used AI tools to make data-management workflows more reliable and useful, including building an agentic document-extraction pipeline that ingests data from over 1,000 reports using LangChain, fine-tuned vision-language models, OCR, and PyTorch. I built evaluation datasets and instrumented agent behavior with Phoenix and OpenTelemetry, improving precision from 50% in a zero-shot approach to 80% with RAG. I also use AI and ML evaluation and observability practices alongside production data pipelines to monitor quality, diagnose failures, and improve downstream data reliability.

question_overrides.pattern: please briefly describe the most significant challenge you have encountered in your work and the approach you took to resolve it.*
question_overrides.answer: A significant challenge was improving the reliability of an AI document-extraction pipeline processing more than 1,000 ESG reports. The initial zero-shot approach achieved only 50% precision. I built evaluation datasets, introduced retrieval-augmented generation, and instrumented the system with Phoenix and OpenTelemetry to identify failure patterns and compare versions. This increased precision to 80% while making the workflow more observable and easier to improve.
